x: They were then lost to sight whilst a lap of some 6 miles was traversed, and when again seen, the field was headed by Sandy, Surrey A.C., with Vickers, Sheffield, in close attendance. Then came Plumb, N.L H., Reddish, H.H.H., and Ludlow, Derby W.C.

Sandy (Surrey A.C.) and Vickers (Sheffield) dashed away at the start and at the five miles mark, at the top of a sharp hill, Sandy had a 200 yds. lead from the bunch who were to be concerned in the finish, consisting of Tommy Green, Plumb, Lloyd Johnson, Edge and Pretti, one of the Italian competitors.

One hundred and sixty-three competitors actually started to the signal of our President over our usual seven miles course, and from the start Johnson (Enfield), Cooper (Woodford Green), Redman (Metropolitan), Plumb (Enfield), Stone (Polytechnic) and Treacher, of ours, were prominent.
Vid.), Christie-Murray (S.W.C.), Tommy Green (Bel.), followed by Plumb (Enfield). A little farther back were Bentley, Bidgood, Rickards and Joe King, all walking together.
